scope.zh: 谁在买、为何买、怎么付钱：九个买家的最新资本开支指引（带证据级别）与财报问答要点，加四个跨公司主题。这里没有收入集中度或客户名单数据。
scope.en: Who buys, why, and how they pay: latest capex outlook (with evidence levels) and Q&A takeaways for nine buyers, plus cross-company themes. Customer-concentration and customer-list data are not included.

primary-read.zh: 已打开并阅读官方原文。
primary-read.en: Official primary document opened and read.

primary-located.zh: 已定位官方来源，细节取自搜索摘要，未逐字核对。
primary-located.en: Official source located; details come from search summaries, not checked verbatim.

secondary-authoritative.zh: 权威机构或行业组织的二手转述。
secondary-authoritative.en: Relayed by an authoritative body or trade press.

secondary.zh: 媒体或聚合站摘要，数字可能因口径或时点不同而冲突。
secondary.en: Press or aggregator summary; figures may conflict by scope or timing.

editorial.zh: 本站对财报问答与来源的编辑归纳，不是已核实结论。
editorial.en: This site’s editorial synthesis of Q&A and sources; not a verified conclusion.

summary.zh: Meta 在2026年Q2业绩中将全年资本开支（含融资租赁本金）收窄至$130–145B；财报问答显示其区分了报告资本开支与合资数据中心建设。
summary.en: In its Q2 2026 results Meta narrowed full-year capex (including finance-lease principal) to $130–145B; the Q&A shows it separates reported capex from joint-venture data-center construction.

facts.zh: Q2资本开支（含融资租赁本金）$31.08B；经营现金流$31.86B；自由现金流$0.784B。
facts.en: Q2 capex including finance-lease principal $31.08B; operating cash flow $31.86B; free cash flow $0.784B.

facts.zh: 此前指引为$125–145B（出处：新闻稿原文）。

caveat.zh: 新闻稿PDF已用文本提取核对上述数字；组件涨价对指引的归因来自二手报道，未在此核对。
caveat.en: The figures above were checked by text extraction from the release PDF; the attribution of the raise to component pricing comes from press coverage and is not checked here.

title.zh: Alphabet：2026年资本开支指引上调至 $195–205B

summary.zh: 多家报道称 Alphabet 在Q2将全年资本开支指引由$180–190B上调至$195–205B，并称2027年将“显著”增加。
summary.en: Several outlets report Alphabet raised 2026 capex guidance from $180–190B to $195–205B in Q2 and said 2027 capex would increase “significantly”.

facts.zh: 报道的Q2资本开支$44.9B，经营现金流$39.1B，自由现金流为负约$5.9B。
facts.en: Reported Q2 capex $44.9B, operating cash flow $39.1B, free cash flow about –$5.9B.

caveat.zh: 未打开 Alphabet 官方业绩材料；部分聚合页仍显示旧的$180–190B，数字请以公司原文为准。
caveat.en: Alphabet’s own results materials were not opened; some aggregator pages still show the older $180–190B, so check the company text.

title.zh: Microsoft：资本开支口径变化，数字不可直接比较
title.en: Microsoft: capex definition changed, figures not directly comparable

summary.zh: 报道称 Microsoft 此前给出2026自然年约$190B，7月后可比口径显示约$175B，原因是新租赁按经营租赁处理且数据中心折旧年限由15年延至25年；公司称剔除会计变化后总投入不变。未给出FY27具体金额，仅称FY27将同比增加。
summary.en: Press reports say Microsoft had guided about $190B for calendar 2026 and the comparable figure after the July report was about $175B, because new leases are being treated as operating leases and data-center useful life was extended from 15 to 25 years; the company says total outlay is unchanged after adjusting. No FY27 amount was given, only that it will rise year over year.

facts.zh: 报道的FY26 Q4资本开支（含融资租赁）约$41B，同比+69%；Azure增速43%。
facts.en: Reported FY26 Q4 capex including finance leases about $41B, up 69%; Azure growth 43%.

sources.label: Hargreaves Lansdown: Microsoft Q4 revenues beat forecasts
Barchart: numbers that matter in Microsoft’s Q2 earnings

caveat.zh: 会计口径变化由二手报道转述，未核对 Microsoft 原文；跨季度比较前先确认口径。
caveat.en: The accounting change is relayed by secondary sources and was not checked against Microsoft’s own text; confirm the definition before comparing across quarters.

title.zh: Amazon：积压订单进入产能规划，资本开支数字未采集
title.en: Amazon: backlog now enters capacity planning; capex figure not captured

summary.zh: 财报问答显示 Amazon 把已知积压纳入规划，并区分合同型与按需需求；Trainium 的采用仍需交付量、软件生态与客户验证，同时继续购买 NVIDIA。本页未采集到可靠的2026年资本开支指引来源。
summary.en: The Q&A shows Amazon folds known backlog into planning and distinguishes contract from on-demand demand; Trainium adoption still depends on volume delivery, software ecosystem and customer proof points while NVIDIA purchases continue. No reliable source for 2026 capex guidance was captured here.

caveat.zh: 此项只依据站内财报问答；金额缺口见方法页“已知缺口”。
caveat.en: Based only on the site’s earnings Q&A; the missing amount is listed under known gaps on the method page.

title.zh: Oracle：自有资本开支与合作方/客户资本分开
title.en: Oracle: Oracle-funded capex separated from partner and customer capital

summary.zh: 问答显示 Oracle 区分硬件自有与供应商租赁模式，长期合同用固定价格或成本传导条款抵御组件涨价，并拒绝给出现金流转正的具体日期。
summary.en: The Q&A shows Oracle distinguishing owned hardware from supplier-rental models, protecting long-term contracts with fixed prices or pass-through clauses against component inflation, and declining a specific cash-flow date.

caveat.zh: 只依据站内财报问答；Stargate 站点进度见能源页。
caveat.en: Based only on the site’s Q&A; Stargate site progress is on the energy page.

title.zh: CoreWeave：延误来自带电厂房交付，而非电力可得性
title.en: CoreWeave: delays came from powered-shell delivery, not power availability

summary.zh: 管理层称基础设施交付延误由带电厂房（powered shell）交付造成，并强调多供应商分散、客户主导的 NVIDIA 需求，未承诺定制 ASIC 路线。
summary.en: Management attributed delivery delays to powered-shell delivery rather than power availability and emphasised provider diversification and customer-led NVIDIA demand without committing to a custom-ASIC roadmap.

caveat.en: Based only on the site’s Q&A.

title.zh: 阿里巴巴：稀缺算力优先分配给高价值模型与推理服务
title.en: Alibaba: scarce compute goes to higher-value model and inference services first

summary.zh: 管理层称企业客户的付费意愿更清晰，所以基础设施目前主要服务企业；对简单GPU出租让位于高价值模型与推理服务；支出受交付时点、CPU需求和组件涨价影响。
summary.en: Management said enterprise customers show clearer willingness to pay, so most infrastructure supports business customers; simple GPU rental yields to higher-value model and inference services; spending was driven by delivery timing, CPU demand and component inflation.

caveat.en: Based only on the site’s Q&A.

title.zh: 腾讯：支出下降归因于芯片可得性，而非需求预期下降
title.en: Tencent: lower spending attributed to chip availability, not lower token-demand expectations

summary.zh: 管理层称瓶颈在中国的加速器受限，CPU与网络通过既有关系保障；预计设备端与云端混合推理逐步迁移。
summary.en: Management said China’s accelerator supply is the constraint, with CPU and networking secured through established relationships, and expected a gradual hybrid device/cloud inference shift.

caveat.en: Based only on the site’s Q&A.

title.zh: 百度：资产减值、融资选择与GPU云毛利
title.en: Baidu: asset impairment, funding choices and GPU-cloud margin

summary.zh: 管理层称部分旧资产不再满足效率需求并更新组合；融资可用租赁或借款；提升GPU云毛利靠产品组合、自研芯片、利用率与规模。
summary.en: Management said some older assets no longer met efficiency needs and refreshed the portfolio; funding may use leasing or borrowing; GPU-cloud margins depend on mix, proprietary chips, utilisation and scale.

caveat.en: Based only on the site’s Q&A.

title.zh: 主题：积压、合同型与按需需求
title.en: Theme: backlog, contract versus on-demand demand

summary.zh: 买家把已知积压放进产能计划，Oracle 用固定价格或传导条款保护长期合同——需求信号越来越多来自合同而非即时用量。
summary.en: Buyers fold known backlog into capacity plans and Oracle protects long-term contracts with fixed prices or pass-through clauses — demand signals increasingly come from contracts rather than spot use.

caveat.zh: 编辑归纳，样本为公司各自的少量问答。
caveat.en: Editorial synthesis from a handful of Q&As per company.

summary.zh: Meta 区分合资数据中心建设与报告资本开支；Oracle 区分自有与合作方资本；百度考虑租赁或借款——“资本开支”口径在买家之间并不一致。
summary.en: Meta separates joint-venture construction from reported capex, Oracle separates its own capital from partner capital, Baidu considers leasing or borrowing — “capex” is not defined the same way across buyers.

caveat.zh: 与Microsoft 口径变化（C03）一起读。
caveat.en: Read together with Microsoft’s definition change (C03).

title.zh: 主题：定制芯片是需求的分流还是补充
title.en: Theme: custom silicon as demand diversion or complement

summary.zh: Amazon 称 Trainium 仍需交付量与软件改善且继续购买 NVIDIA；Microsoft 保留外部供应商以保持成本弹性；CoreWeave 强调客户主导的 NVIDIA 需求。
summary.en: Amazon says Trainium needs volume and software progress while NVIDIA purchases continue; Microsoft keeps external suppliers for cost flexibility; CoreWeave stresses customer-led NVIDIA demand.

title.zh: 主题：组件涨价进入资本开支
title.en: Theme: component inflation flowing into capex

summary.zh: Meta 的上调归因于组件价格（二手报道）；Microsoft 报道称含$25B组件涨价；Amazon、CoreWeave、阿里、Oracle 的问答都提到成本传导，但没有人把涨价与容量增量完全拆开。
summary.en: Meta’s raise is attributed to component pricing (press coverage); Microsoft is reported to include $25B of component pricing; Amazon, CoreWeave, Alibaba and Oracle Q&As mention cost pass-through, but none fully separates inflation from capacity added.

caveat.zh: 部分数字来自二手报道（见C01、C03）。
caveat.en: Some numbers come from press coverage (see C01, C03).
